title: Settings search sends 'license' and 'credits' to About, which contains neither
what_happened: The About section declares keywords ['version','license','credits','updates','build'] (settings_catalog.dart:205-214). Typing 'license' into the Settings search box filters the section list down to exactly one entry, About -- and the About page has no licence text, no third-party/credits list, and no build number. The search promises information the destination does not have.
expected: Either About carries a licence + open-source-credits block (Flutter's showLicensePage is one line) and the build number, or those keywords come out of the catalog so the search does not lie.
repro: Settings > search box > type 'license'. Only 'About' is listed. Open it: version 6.1.0, tagline, 3 links, Platform/OS/Dart rows. Nothing else.
evidence: tree after typing 'license': the section list collapses to a single 'About' entry; the About page tree is Skotiq / Version 6.1.0 / Advanced astrophotography suite / GitHub / Documentation / Discord / System Information / Platform / OS Version / Dart Version.
proposed_fix: Add a licence/credits row (showLicensePage) and show the full build string; keep the keywords.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed live and in source. Typing 'license' in the Settings search collapses the section list to exactly one entry, About (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-06.png). Opening it gives: Skotiq / Version 6.1.0 / 'Advanced astrophotography suite' / GitHub / Documentation / Report an Issue / System Information (Platform linux, OS Version, Dart Version 3.12.1). No licence text, no credits, no build number. settings_catalog.dart:205-214 still declares keywords ['version','license','credits','updates','build']; about_settings.dart (read in full) has no showLicensePage/LicenseRegistry and prints only appVersion.version, never AppVersionInfo.buildNumber. Location as cited is accurate.

title: Filter Focus Offsets silently omits the filter you just added -- you cannot set an offset for it without saving and re-opening the editor
what_happened: In Settings > Equipment Profiles > (profile) > Edit, I added a 4th filter 'SII' with the + button and typed its name. Filter Configuration then showed 4 chips (Lum, Ha, OIII, SII) but the Filter Focus Offsets card directly underneath still listed only 3 rows (Lum, Ha, OIII) -- no offset input exists for SII. The section is built from _filterControllers, but nothing calls setState when a filter-name field changes, so the offsets list lags one interaction behind. Pressing Save and re-entering Edit made the SII row appear. Same lag on the very first filter: the offsets section does not appear at all until some other widget forces a rebuild.
expected: Naming a filter should immediately add its focus-offset row; the two lists describe the same filters and must stay in sync within one edit session.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > New Profile > Edit > Filter Configuration '+' > type a filter name > look at Filter Focus Offsets: the new filter is missing. Save, re-open Edit: now present.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rss-49.png -- Filter Configuration row reads Lum | Ha | OIII | SII while Filter Focus Offsets below lists Lum, Ha, OIII only. Confirmed in tree output too (4 filter fields, 3 offset rows).
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/profile_details_helpers.dart:154-165 (_buildFilterOffsetRows reads _filterControllers) with no onChanged->setState on the filter-name TextFields in profile_details_rendering.dart:449-500
location_wrong: First half right (profile_details_helpers.dart:154-165 is the offsets loop). Second half off: the filter-name TextField that lacks onChanged is _EditableFilterChip in profile_controls.dart:306-321, not profile_details_rendering.dart:449-500 -- that range only instantiates the chip (:486-492).
proposed_fix: Add onChanged: (_) => setState(() {}) to the filter-name fields (or drive both lists off a single ValueNotifier).
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on a fresh profile. In Edit, typing 'Lum' into the pre-seeded filter chip produced NO Filter Focus Offsets section at all -- it appeared only after I pressed '+', which forced a rebuild. Then with chips 'Lum | Ha', typing 'Ha' into the second chip left Filter Focus Offsets listing only 'Lum' with no input for Ha (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-24.png; full page /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-27.png). Save + re-open Edit made both rows appear (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-28.png). Mechanism as described: profile_details_helpers.dart:155-166 builds the offset rows from _filterControllers[i].text and the filter-name TextField has no onChanged, so nothing calls setState when the name is typed.

title: Appliance Catalogs on the desktop app talks about 'the phone's own planetarium catalogs' and offers no way to connect anything
what_happened: Settings > Appliance Catalogs on the Linux desktop build renders a title, the subtitle 'Download and verify the rig's plate-solve / star catalogs', and one info panel: 'Connect to a remote appliance to manage its catalogs. This is separate from the phone's own planetarium catalogs.' There is no phone here -- this is the desktop app -- and the page carries no connect button, no appliance picker and no link to Remote Access, so it is an entirely inert settings leaf whose only sentence is about a different platform.
expected: Say 'This machine's own planetarium catalogs' (or 'this device's'), and either give the page an action that reaches the appliance-connection flow or hide the section on builds that are not acting as a remote client.
repro: Settings > search 'catalog' > Appliance Catalogs (desktop Linux build, no appliance paired).
location_wrong: The finding gave no file. Precise location: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/rig_catalog_settings.dart:276-289.
proposed_fix: Platform-neutral wording plus a 'Connect an appliance' action that routes to Remote Access, or gate the section on an active appliance connection.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on the Linux desktop build with no appliance connected. Settings > Appliance Catalogs renders exactly three strings and nothing else: 'Appliance Catalogs', 'Download and verify the rig's plate-solve / star catalogs', and one info panel 'Connect to a remote appliance to manage its catalogs. This is separate from the phone's own planetarium catalogs.' The tree shows no button, picker or link anywhere on the page. Source confirms: rig_catalog_settings.dart:281-289, the `if (backend == null)` branch renders a bare _Info with that text and no action, and the desktop build hard-codes 'the phone's'.

title: Log Export dumps 18.8 MB into the home Documents folder without warning, ignoring both the configured data directory and the app's own exports/ folder
what_happened: Settings > Logs > Export wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/skotiq_logs_2026-08-02T11-08-20.txt: 18,829,614 bytes, 142,921 lines, containing every rotated log file back to 2026-07-27 -- from a sandboxed instance launched with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-system/data. There is no file picker, no size estimate, and no confirmation; the only notice is the (invisible, see the snackbar finding) message 'Logs exported to: <path>'. It also does not use ~/Documents/Skotiq/exports/, which is where the app puts its other exports.
expected: Ask where to save (the app already uses a native save dialog for profile export), state the size, and default to the same exports/ directory as everything else. A user clicking Export to attach a log to a bug report does not expect an 18 MB file in the root of Documents.
evidence: File listing above; head of the file shows '=== /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs/skotiq.log.2026-07-27 ==='; ~/Documents/Skotiq/exports/ contains only unrelated CSVs.
proposed_fix: Use the same FilePicker save flow as profile export, default to the exports/ directory under the resolved data dir, and offer 'visible entries only' vs 'full history'.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Settings > Logs > Export, from an instance launched with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/v2-settings-system/data, wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/skotiq_logs_2026-08-03T17-11-30.txt -- 19,489,798 bytes, 147,939 lines. No file picker, no size estimate, no confirmation; the only notice is the line 'Logs exported to: <path>'. The file concatenates every rotated on-disk log back to 2026-07-28 (section headers '=== /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs/skotiq.log.2026-07-28 ===' through 2026-08-03, then '=== In-memory Dart log entries ==='), so it also reads the real user log dir rather than the sandbox. ~/Documents/Skotiq/exports/ holds only unrelated CSV/HTML session exports. Location is right: log_viewer.dart:241-276 _exportLogs, path built at :262 as '${docsDir.path}/skotiq_logs_$timestamp.txt' with no picker.

title: Duplicate happily creates two profiles with byte-identical names, while Import de-duplicates -- so the profile list can show rows nothing can tell apart
what_happened: Duplicating the same profile twice and accepting the offered name both times produced ids 4 and 5, both named 'Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy)'. The list renders two identical rows (same title, same 'No description', same icon) with nothing to distinguish them, and the status-bar profile chip shows only a name, so once one of them is active you cannot tell which. The importer, by contrast, does resolve collisions -- importing a profile named 'Audit Rig Alpha' over an existing one produced 'Audit Rig Alpha (1)'. Two code paths, two different rules.
expected: One rule: reject or auto-suffix a colliding name everywhere. Duplicate should offer '(Copy 2)' the second time, exactly as Import offers '(1)'.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > overflow > Duplicate > Duplicate (accept the pre-filled name). Repeat. sqlite3 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' -> two rows with the same name.
evidence: DB: 4|Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy) and 5|Local Work Do Not Lose (Copy); tree shows two identical list rows.
where: the duplicate handler's default name generation vs the importer's collision resolution
proposed_fix: Route both through one uniqueName(base) helper, and add a UNIQUE index on equipment_profiles.name if names are meant to be identifiers.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Duplicating 'Adv Rig One' five times, accepting the pre-filled name each time, produced ids 2,3,4,5,6 all named exactly 'Adv Rig One (Copy)' (sqlite3), rendered as five visually identical rows with the same icon and no subtitle (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2-31.png). The offered name is a fixed '${profile.name} (Copy)' built at screen_shell.dart:368 with no collision check, whereas the importer resolves collisions with a '(n)' suffix. P3 is fair -- usability/consistency, not data loss.
